title: Purchasing Administrator
description:
Mechanical & Electrical products Data handling & administration High-volume purchasing
Leeds
up to 35,000
Are you highly organised, detail-oriented and confident working with large volumes of product and purchasing data?
We are working with an established business operating within the mechanical and electrical products market and they are looking to appoint a Purchasing Administrator to support the purchasing function and bring greater structure, accuracy and consistency to their product and order data.
This is a role where attention to detail really matters. You will be responsible for working through product information, establishing and maintaining SKUs, checking order numbers and ensuring purchasing data is correctly recorded, organised and accessible.
The role:

You will take ownership of a range of administrative and data-focused activities, including:
- Creating, checking and maintaining SKU and product information
- Establishing correct product and order numbers across a wide range of mechanical and electrical products
- Sorting, organising and cleansing purchasing data
- Maintaining accurate product and supplier records
- Checking information for discrepancies, duplication and errors
- Supporting purchase order administration and processing
- Updating internal systems and spreadsheets with accurate information
- Helping to improve the structure, accuracy and consistency of purchasing data

The person:

This opportunity will suit someone who is methodical, analytical and exceptionally organised, with the patience and attention to detail required to work through large volumes of information.
You will ideally have experience within a purchasing, procurement, supply chain, stock, product administration or data administration environment.
You will be comfortable working with:
- Large volumes of data and product information
- SKU, product and order numbers
- Data checking, sorting and reconciliation
- Multiple product lines where accuracy is critical

You will take pride in getting the detail right, be confident identifying inconsistencies and enjoy bringing order and structure to complex information.
Why this role?
This is an excellent opportunity to join an established business where you can play an important role in improving the accuracy and organisation of its purchasing data.
If you are looking for a role where your attention to detail, organisation and ability to manage complex product information will genuinely make a difference, we would be keen to hear from you. Please submit your CV quoting reference 10527.

title: Operations Assistant - Stock, Purchasing & Logistics
description:
Stock & Purchasing Coordinator / Operations Assistanrt
East Leeds LS14 - Hybrid working available after probation
30,000 - 35,000 Permanent Monday - Friday, 8.30am - 5pm

A well-established and growing business is looking for a Stock & Purchasing Coordinator to join its Operations team.

This is a varied role combining stock administration, purchasing, supplier management, order processing and logistics coordination. You'll be responsible for keeping stock information accurate, monitoring orders and deliveries, resolving queries and working closely with internal teams and external suppliers.

The role would suit an experienced administrator who enjoys working with systems, stock, orders and suppliers and is looking for a long-term opportunity within a friendly and established business.

What's on offer?
- 30,000 - 35,000 salary
- Permanent position
- Monday - Friday, 8.30am - 5pm, 37.5 hours per week
- Hybrid working available after probation, with the opportunity to work from home 1-2 days per week
- Annual bonus scheme
- 25 days' holiday, increasing with length of service
- Option to purchase additional annual leave
- Employee Assistance Programme
- Cycle to work scheme
- Free office parking
- Enhanced sick pay
- Life assurance
- Smart casual dress code

The Role

Working as part of the Operations team, your responsibilities will include:
- Coordinating incoming stock and monitoring expected delivery dates
- Updating internal systems with stock and supplier information
- Checking supplier pricing and investigating discrepancies
- Raising and processing purchase and stock orders
- Monitoring outstanding orders and deliveries
- Liaising with suppliers to ensure orders are delivered as expected
- Coordinating the movement and processing of stock where required
- Assisting with regular stock checks and system reconciliations
- Investigating and resolving stock, order and invoice queries
- Monitoring customer and supplier orders through to completion
- Supporting internal processes relating to product information and certification
- Working with internal teams to improve systems and processes
- Providing information and updates to colleagues across the business
- Working closely with the sales team to ensure excellent customer service
- Providing general administrative support to the Operations function

About You

We're looking for someone who is organised, commercially aware and comfortable working with stock, orders, suppliers and computer systems.

You will ideally have:

Previous experience in an administrative, stock, purchasing, logistics, supply chain or order processing role
Experience working with a stock, purchasing, inventory or ERP system
Good understanding of administrative and order management processes
Strong attention to detail and good numerical skills
Excellent written and verbal communication skills
Confident telephone manner
Good Microsoft Office skills, particularly Excel
Strong organisational and time management skills
Ability to work accurately in a busy environment
Good problem-solving skills and the ability to investigate and resolve issues
Ability to work independently and use your own initiative
A positive, flexible approach and the ability to work well as part of a team
Experience within a technical, manufacturing, construction, distribution or supply-chain environment would be advantageous, although this is not essential.

Travel

The role is primarily office based in East Leeds - LS14

There will be occasional travel to other UK locations for stock checks, approximately 6 times per year. These visits will generally involve 1-2 overnight stays, with accommodation and business expenses paid by the company.

A full UK driving licence is preferred.

Working Pattern

Monday - Friday, 8.30am - 5pm, with a one-hour lunch break.

The position is initially office based, with 1-2 days' home working available following successful completion of probation, subject to line manager approval.

This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced administrator looking to develop their career within stock, purchasing, logistics or operations with an established and supportive employer.

Red Recruitment is recruiting Customer Service Advisors in Leeds city centre to join our client, an award-winning customer management company that has achieved GOLD awards from both Investors in People and Investors in Customers.

In this role, you will provide telephone support to enforcement agents attending customers properties in relation to outstanding utility debt. You will complete structured fact-finding checks, review account information and ensure the correct legal, regulatory and operational procedures have been followed before any action is taken.

You will help ensure every case is handled fairly, accurately and with appropriate consideration for the customer s individual circumstances.

- Contract Type: Permanent
- Location: Leeds city centre
- Free parking
- Health and wellbeing programme
- Monthly bonus scheme

- 33 days annual leave, including bank holidays and your birthday

- Full support and training provided
- Career progression opportunities

Key Responsibilities of a Customer Service Advisor:
- Provide telephone and operational support to enforcement agents attending customers properties
- Complete a structured fact-finding process with agents during live property visits

Key Skills and Experience of a Customer Service Advisor:
- Previous experience in customer service, contact centre, operations support, collections or a regulated environment

- Strong questioning and fact-finding skills, with the confidence to obtain accurate information
- Excellent verbal communication skills and the ability to provide clear guidance over the telephone
- Strong attention to detail and the ability to follow structured procedures accurately

description:
Personal Assistant to Sales Director

Role Overview

Are you highly organised, proactive and confident working closely with senior management?

We are looking for a Personal Assistant to support our Sales Director and wider commercial team, providing high-quality administrative, organisational and sales support within one of the fastest-growing specialised Truck Rental companies in the country.

This is more than a traditional administration role. You will become a key support to the Sales Director, helping manage their diary, meetings, customer information and day-to-day workload. A key part of the role will involve attending sales meetings, taking accurate notes, recording actions and ensuring all relevant information is inputted onto our CRM and internal systems.

You will need to be organised, commercially aware and confident dealing with customers and colleagues at all levels. This is an excellent opportunity for someone with PA, Executive Assistant, Sales Support or Senior Administration experience who wants to develop within a fast-paced and growing business.

Key Responsibilities

Provide day-to-day PA and administrative support to the Sales Director.

Manage diaries, appointments, meetings and customer visits.

Attend sales meetings and take clear, accurate notes of discussions, decisions and agreed actions.

Input meeting notes, customer updates, actions and sales information accurately onto the CRM and internal systems.

Maintain accurate and up-to-date customer records, contacts and sales information.

Monitor actions following meetings and ensure key tasks are followed up and completed.

Prepare meeting agendas, reports, presentations and other sales documentation.

Support the Sales Director with quotations, contracts, correspondence and customer documentation.

Handle telephone calls and emails, dealing with queries professionally or directing them to the appropriate person.

Coordinate with workshop, logistics, finance and other internal departments on behalf of the Sales Director.

Assist with customer visits, sales events and promotional activity in conjunction with the wider team.

Arrange travel, accommodation and other requirements for business meetings and visits.

Help monitor sales opportunities and ensure relevant information is recorded accurately within company systems.

Maintain confidentiality when dealing with commercially sensitive and customer information.

Keep up to date with company products and services to provide accurate information to customers and colleagues.

Provide general administrative and organisational support to help the Sales Director and sales team operate effectively.

Required Skills & Experience

Essential

Proven experience in a PA, Personal Assistant, Executive Assistant, Sales Support or senior administration role.

Excellent organisational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities.

Strong written and verbal communication skills.

Excellent note-taking skills and a high level of accuracy when recording and inputting information.

Confident using Microsoft Office, particularly Outlook, Word and Excel.

Comfortable using CRM, databases and other computerised systems.

Strong attention to detail and ability to maintain accurate records.

Professional and confident when communicating with customers, colleagues and senior management.

Ability to work independently, use initiative and anticipate the needs of the Sales Director.

Friendly, professional and commercially aware approach.

Good GCSEs or equivalent in Maths and English.

Desirable

Previous experience supporting a Sales Director, Managing Director or senior manager.

Experience within sales, commercial administration or customer service.

Experience within the HGV, truck rental, transport or automotive sector.

Previous experience using CRM systems.

Experience preparing sales reports, presentations or meeting documentation.

Understanding of sales processes and commercial operations.

Benefits

23 days paid annual leave + bank holidays

Company workplace pension scheme (auto-enrolment)

Free on-site parking

Training and career progression opportunities

Death in service (after qualifying period)

All our information is available in accessible formats. Please contact the Recruitment team recruitment.lypft@nhs.net Attached to this advert is our candidates guide to values-based recruitment and supporting guidance on how to make a successful application. If you require a reasonable adjustment, please contact the Recruitment Team or see the attached candidate guide to reasonable adjustments. title: Receptionist/ Telephonist
description: Elmwood Family Doctors is a large, forward-thinking GP practice serving our local community across two sites in Holmfirth and Meltham . We are looking to recruit an enthusiastic, friendly and motivated Receptionist/Telephonist to join our supportive and dedicated team. Hours of Work (19 hours per week) Monday: 8:00am to 6:00pm Tuesday: 8:00am to 1:00pm Wednesday: 3:00pm to 8:00pm As the first point of contact for our patients, you will play an important role in delivering excellent customer service and helping ensure patients receive the support and care they need. Strong communication skills, a positive attitude and the ability to work effectively as part of a team are essential. At Elmwood Family Doctors, we pride ourselves on being a friendly, welcoming and supportive practice where staff are valued and encouraged to develop. Holmfirth and Meltham are fantastic places to live and work, offering excellent schools, a strong sense of community and a vibrant programme of local events and festivals. Surrounded by the beautiful Pennine countryside, the area also benefits from excellent amenities and convenient transport links to Leeds, Manchester and Sheffield. If you enjoy working with people, thrive in a busy environment and want to make a real difference to healthcare within your local community, we would love to hear from you. The role involves supporting patients with their enquiries, booking appointments, and signposting them to the most appropriate services. This is predominantly carried out over the telephone, alongside providing a welcoming and professional face-to-face service at the reception desk. Successful candidates will spend part of each shift working within our dedicated telephone team, supported by friendly colleagues and ongoing training. Strong customer service skills and the ability to work effectively as part of a team are essential. The role also includes a variety of administrative tasks. While full training will be provided, good IT skills are essential, and previous administrative experience would be advantageous. We are looking for someone who is approachable, organised and motivated, with excellent communication skills and a positive team-focused attitude. Experience in a similar role within the NHS or healthcare setting would be beneficial, but is not essential. The role involves supporting the delivery of a high-quality GP service by acting as a first point of contact for patients and visitors. You will provide a friendly, efficient and accurate service, assisting with appointment booking, patient enquiries and a range of administrative duties. Key responsibilities include (but are not limited to): Welcoming patients and handling enquiries at the reception desk Responding to telephone enquiries and directing patients to the most appropriate service Booking and managing patient appointments Using clinical IT systems (including SystmOne) to carry out administrative tasks such as patient registrations, updating records, and scanning correspondence into digital records Processing, repeat prescriptions and clinical information Supporting clinical staff, including chaperoning patients where appropriate Maintaining clinical areas, including re-stocking rooms Hours and Location This is a part-time role worked over a 3-day shift pattern, with shifts scheduled across the week to meet the needs of the service. The role is based across both of our sites in Holmfirth and Meltham , and staff are required to work flexibly between the two locations. This provides the opportunity to work closely with a wide range of colleagues and patients, and to develop a varied and rewarding role. Due to the nature of the role and the importance of teamwork and patient interaction, this position is fully on-site. The successful candidate may need to be able to travel between both sites.

title: Administrator
description: THE PHARMACIST NETWORK Administrator Job Description Reports to: Business Operations Coordinator Direct reports: None Location: Newcastle, Hybrid Working pattern: Full-time, Monday-Friday 9am-5pm Salary: £26,000 £27,000 The Administrator keeps the day-to-day administration of the TPN central team running. It is a broad, hands-on support role: managing shared inboxes and correspondence, maintaining accurate records across TPN's systems, preparing documentation, and coordinating the routine processes that keep a busy operations function moving. The role suits someone organised and IT literate who is comfortable owning routine work end to end, spotting when something has been missed, and keeping records clean without being chased. Key accountabilities: Manage TPN's shared administrative inboxes triaging enquiries, responding to routine correspondence, and routing what needs a specialist to the right person. Maintain accurate, current records across TPN's systems and shared drives data entry, file management, version control, and routine housekeeping. Prepare and format documents, templates, reports, and correspondence to a consistent standard. Support the compliance administration around TPN's workforce collating and filing documentation, tracking what is outstanding, and flagging gaps for the responsible manager. Coordinate meetings and diary logistics scheduling, room and video setup, circulating papers, and taking and distributing notes where required. Provide administrative support to the wider central team on projects and recurring operational tasks. Handle sensitive and confidential information in line with GDPR and TPN's data handling requirements. Contribute to improving administrative processes surfacing what is slow, duplicated, or manual, and helping tidy it up. This list is not exhaustive; the role may include other administrative responsibilities as the central team develops. Skills and experience Essential skills: Organisation and prioritisation managing a varied workload across competing requests without dropping detail IT literacy confident across Microsoft 365 (Outlook, Word, Excel, Teams, SharePoint) and quick to pick up new systems Accuracy and attention to detail, particularly in data entry and record keeping Clear written and verbal communication, including professional correspondence with colleagues and external contacts Discretion and confidentiality when handling personal and sensitive information Self-direction and initiative - comfortable organising and managing your own workload. Essential experience: Prior administrative experience in an office, operations, or business support setting Experience maintaining records or databases with a high standard of accuracy Experience managing a shared inbox or handling routine correspondence on behalf of a team Desirable: Healthcare, primary care, pharmacy, or NHS-adjacent experience Experience supporting a compliance, HR, or recruitment administration process Familiarity with CRM, ATS, or workflow systems (TPN is moving onto the Zoho ecosystem) Experience working in a hybrid team across multiple sites

title: Operations & Compliance Administrator
description: PriDerm Community Dermatology Service is looking for an experienced and highly organised Operations & Compliance Administrator to join our busy community dermatology team. This is a varied role that goes beyond traditional administration. You will play an important part in supporting the day-to-day operation, monitoring, compliance and continuous improvement of our service. We are looking for someone who is confident working with data, reports and administrative systems, has excellent attention to detail and enjoys making sure processes are followed correctly. You will need to be comfortable identifying problems, raising concerns, monitoring actions and helping to find practical solutions. This is an excellent opportunity for someone who wants to develop their experience in operations, compliance, audit, reporting and service improvement within a healthcare environment. Operations & Compliance Administrator Main Duties Responsible for supporting the day-to-day operations of a busy community dermatology service, ensuring administrative processes are accurate, efficient and compliant with policies and healthcare requirements. Key duties include managing referrals, waiting lists, appointments and patient records; maintaining spreadsheets, databases and compliance trackers; carrying out audits and quality checks; monitoring service performance and producing reports; identifying errors, risks and areas for improvement; following up outstanding actions; supporting management with accurate data and reporting; and helping to implement process improvements. The role also involves maintaining confidentiality, ensuring information governance requirements are met, and working collaboratively with clinical and administrative teams to maintain high standards of patient care and service delivery. What will you be doing?Operations and Administration Supporting the effective day-to-day administration and operation of the community dermatology service. Managing referrals, waiting lists, appointments, correspondence and patient records. Ensuring administrative processes are completed accurately, efficiently and within required timescales. When required, supporting or overseeing the day-to-day work of the administration team, ensuring priorities are managed effectively and tasks are completed. Maintaining accurate spreadsheets, databases, trackers and monitoring systems. Supporting month-end processes and providing accurate information to management. Compliance and Quality Monitoring compliance with PriDerm policies, procedures and service requirements. Carrying out regular audits and quality checks to ensure processes are being followed correctly. Checking records and administrative activity for accuracy and completeness. Maintaining compliance trackers and action logs. Identifying errors, gaps, risks or areas where processes are not being followed and escalating these appropriately. Following up outstanding actions to ensure they are completed within agreed timescales. Supporting the preparation and maintenance of evidence required for audits, reviews and compliance monitoring. Supporting the implementation of new policies, procedures and operational processes. Reporting and Monitoring Producing regular operational and compliance reports using Excel and other systems. Monitoring service activity, waiting lists, referrals, appointments and other key performance information. Identifying trends, discrepancies or areas of concern within the data. Providing accurate information and reports to management to support decision-making. Maintaining accurate and up-to-date monitoring systems and ensuring information is readily available when required. Service Improvement Identifying opportunities to improve administrative processes and the way the service operates. Working with colleagues to implement improvements and monitor their effectiveness. Supporting investigations into administrative errors, process failures or areas of non-compliance where required. Taking ownership of agreed actions and seeing them through to completion. Working collaboratively with the wider team to promote high standards of quality, accuracy and compliance. Working hours Monday - Thursday: until 5:30pm Friday: until 4:30pm Start time: To be confirmed Please note: This position does not include an NHS pension. About PriDerm Community Dermatology Service PriDerm Community Dermatology Service provides dermatology care to the local community in North Kirklees . We are a busy service delivering a range of community dermatology clinics and supporting patients throughout their care pathway. Our administrative and operational teams play a vital role in ensuring that patients receive an efficient, well-organised and high-quality service.

title: Finance Administrator
description: PURPOSE OF THE ROLE: The Finance Assistant works in a small team dealing with general financial administrative duties in a timely fashion. The postholder will be numerate and enjoy working in a finance-focused environment. They will have strong computer skills, particularly in the use of excel and computerised account systems. Ideally the Finance Assistant will have worked within Primary Care or the NHS, although this is not essential. Working hours Flexible working hours to cover the full time equivalent of 1.5 cover, to be discussed at Interview stage. The Finance Assistant is responsible for: The accurate and timely production of financial information Processing financial information as it arrives in the inbox / post and accurately responding. Paying invoices and ensuring they are accompanied by appropriate documentation Supporting supplier payments Day-to-day communication within the finance team and with the wider organisation. Key Responsibilities Monitor communication and information flow into the Finance department via post, email, telephone, or other channels and respond appropriately Input sales and purchase invoices and credit notes into the system, ensuring correct financial coding is applied Ensure that all relevant documentation related to payment of invoices is accurate and up to date before payment is processed, such as purchase orders and delivery notes, bank details and company addresses Supporting supplier payments, ensuring they are processed within agreed terms. These payments can be significant in value, so the post holder must be accurate and experienced in handling high value payments, referring to the Finance Manager when necessary Produce regular aged debtor and creditor reports Credit control and debt management for all customers including producing customer statements and reconciliations, supporting the Finance team and working alongside the Finance Manager to resolve outstanding aged debtors Maintain effective relationships with internal and external stakeholders and respond to first line queries regarding financial issues Monthly reconciliation of supplier statements to the purchase ledger, working to resolve any queries or differences that may arise within the roles delegated authority Supporting with banking reconciliations Day to day management of petty cash Assisting and supporting the Finance Manager in a variety of tasks and procedures -especially at month and year end Contribute as an effective team member within the Finance Services team, supporting the achievement of finance objectives, including the evaluation of processes Provide support to the external and internal audit processes Liaise between HR and the external payroll provider. Provide accurate payroll data. General office administrative duties such as filing bank statements, invoices and other documents. Provide support to other members of the team as required Develop strong, professional relationships with colleagues to help create a positive working environment Promote an efficient and positive image of the organisation for all suppliers and customers Comply with strict financial timetables, contributing to an efficient and effective financial accounting service Undertake any other duties as agreed with the Finance Manager, in order to meet the needs of the organisation.

title: Practice Administrator
description: Warrengate Medical Centre is a busy and friendly town-centre Doctors surgery providing a full range of NHS services to a list size of more than 11,000 patients. We are a high achieving friendly training Practice with an excellent reputation situated in the Centre of Wakefield close to transport links and local amenities. We are committed to maintaining our high standard of patient care and customer service in a friendly and professional environment and we are currently looking a part time Practice Administrator to join our friendly team. This is a permanent position. The working patterns required are detailed below, however flexibility is required for covering annual leave and sickness absences. Wednesday : 8am - 4.30pm Thursday : 10am - 6.30pm Friday 8am - 4.30pm 5 Great reasons to join our Warrengate team: Inclusive and diverse workforce As a training practice we support and encourage career development Supportive team environment Automatic enrolment into NHS pension scheme and access to NHS discounts and benefits Staff wellbeing is at the heart of our family practice ethos. The candidates we are seeking should be experienced in delivering excellent customer service, maintaining professionalism, discretion and confidentiality at all times and able to work well under pressure both independently, and as part of a team. You will need to have excellent communication and organisational skills, together with a caring and solution focused approach to patient related problems. The main duties will be answering phones and dealing with patients face to face, care navigating patients to the most appropriate person / service to help, dealing with repeat prescriptions, scanning, managing patient related tasks as directed by the Practice team. You will have the ability to remain calm in difficult situations as well as having the initiative to identify outstanding workload and support the team in completing this. Flexibility to cover colleagues annual leave and sickness is essential. Full training will be given but Medical Administration and Receptionist experience in a similar environment would be advantageous. For more details about this position please see Job Description and Person Specification For further information please contact Julie Woods, Office Manager on 01924 371011 Duties will include, but are not limited to: Booking appointments for patients following care navigation ensuring patients access the most appropriate services within the practice Scanning and workflowing incoming correspondence within the clinical system Dealing with general enquiries from patients and prioritising the management of these Dealing with repeat prescription orders and prescription queries Managing your time and workload efficiently Assisting with the smooth running of clinics and surgeries Providing help and advice to all visitors to the surgery and the building Registration of new patients to the Practice Process patients change of address and contact details within the clinical system Dealing with tasks that clinicians may assign to you in an effective and timely manner Covering colleagues shifts in the event of sickness or annual leave Effective communication between staff, the practice, patients and other agencies Understanding and implementation of the practice protocols and procedures Carrying out the daily tasks set for you by the Office Manager Attending training and staff meetings as required Supporting with other reasonable duties as required Follow the practices Infection Prevention & Control policies and protocols

title: GP Surgery Receptionist

The role is for 37 hours a week. However, flexibility is essential as you will also be expected to cover for holidays and sickness. Pay rate is competitive and you will receive 6 weeks holiday plus bank holiday. Previous experience as a Receptionist in General Practice or another busy reception environment is essential.
